title: A Good CREPE needs more than just Sugar: Investigating Biases in Compositional Vision-Language Benchmarks

bias_targets.methodology: Using 'blind' text-only language models to compute token-length differences and log-likelihoods (plausibility) of positive versus negative captions, revealing that vision-language benchmarks contain distributional asymmetries that allow them to be solved via unimodal shortcuts rather than true multimodal compositional reasoning.

Comparing the performance of standard vision-language models (e.g., CLIP) against unimodal baselines that completely ignore the image input, demonstrating that models rely on text-only shortcuts (like length and plausibility) instead of joint image-text understanding.
